newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends near low, Brent pulls back with US.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends near low, Brent pulls back with US.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed near the low on Monday in a lacklustre performance that failed to penetrate any significant resistance despite support from firmer Brent, brokers said.
Front-month July gas oil settled at $160.25 a tonne, $1.75 firmer, after touching a high of $161.

August Brent crude futures were trading at $17.76 a barrel at 1701 GMT, nine cents firmer than Friday. It eased to to a low of $17.74 in late afternoon in sympathy with August crude's fall to a low of $18.93 on NYMEX.
"Any rally just got sold into," a gas oil trader said.
"Gas oil lifted with Brent but later gasoline in the U.S. failed to rally and gas oil followed that lead."
Brent's morning strength was on the back of concern over tension between the United Nations and Iraq, traders said.
The U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution over the weekend threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it does not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.
It also suspended until the end of October regular 60-day reviews of current sanctions.
But some brokers said support from the Iraq situation would fade without fresh news. OPEC gave little direction.
Ministers were starting to arrive in Vienna for this week's OPEC conference.
Traders saw support for August Brent at $17.68 and then $17.49. Resistance was around $17.97.
